monitor_list.name: Unnamed new LNG terminal proposal (pre-development stage)
monitor_list.sponsor: Unidentified — referenced only by DOE Secretary Sharon Garin, no developer/location named
monitor_list.why_below_threshold: DOE Secretary Sharon Garin stated in Oct 2025 that 'one new terminal proposal is in the pre-development stage' while explaining the Philippines has excess LNG regas capacity and is not prioritizing new Luzon terminals (may eventually look at Visayas/Mindanao). No developer name, exact location, or concrete step was reported in any outlet found (BusinessWorld, Manila Times, TradingView/Reuters syndication, World Energy News, interaksyon). Fails tight threshold on (a) named sponsor and (b) concrete step; worth a web check in a future batch once/if a developer surfaces.

duplicates_confirmed.name_in_press: San Miguel / Ilijan LNG import terminal (Excelerate FSRU NTP, later AG&P PHLNG)
duplicates_confirmed.maps_to_covered: Philippines LNG Terminal / AG&P PHLNG at Batangas (operating)
duplicates_confirmed.evidence: The Ilijan-area import terminal built and commissioned by AG&P/Linseed Field Corp at Batangas Bay is the same facility GEM already tracks as 'Philippines LNG Terminal' (aka PHLNG, AG&P LNG Terminal). Excelerate's 2019 FSRU NTP at this site never proceeded past the DOE approval stage and was superseded by AG&P's own project; no separate operating Excelerate facility exists at Ilijan. (LNG Prime, Manila Standard, tanknewsinternational.com, agpglobal.com — see url_verifications).

duplicates_confirmed.name_in_press: Linseed Field Corp / Linseed Field Power Corp Batangas LNG terminal
duplicates_confirmed.maps_to_covered: Philippines LNG Terminal / AG&P PHLNG at Batangas (operating)
duplicates_confirmed.evidence: Linseed Field Power Corp is the AG&P-affiliated project company that built and owns the Batangas/Ilijan import terminal now tracked as GEM's 'Philippines LNG Terminal.' March 2024/Jan 2025 news that Meralco PowerGen (MGen), Therma NatGas Power and San Miguel Global Power jointly acquired Linseed Field Corp confirms it is the SAME facility, not a new one (Manila Standard, BusinessWorld, Chambers and Partners, LNG Prime).

duplicates_confirmed.name_in_press: Excelerate Energy 'Filipinas LNG Gateway' / 'open access' FSRU at Batangas Bay
duplicates_confirmed.evidence: GMA News, DOE press release, and Maritime Executive/JPT-SPE coverage of Excelerate's open-access FSRU (150,000 cbm, 9.5 km offshore Batangas Bay) all describe the same 'Filipinas LNG Gateway' project already tracked by GEM as under construction.

duplicates_confirmed.name_in_press: Meralco PowerGen (MGen) / Therma NatGas / San Miguel Global Power LNG terminal acquisition
duplicates_confirmed.maps_to_covered: Philippines LNG Terminal / AG&P PHLNG at Batangas (operating) [via Linseed Field Corp acquisition]
duplicates_confirmed.evidence: The $3.3bn deal closed Jan 2025 is an ownership change (acquisition of Linseed Field Corp) at the EXISTING covered terminal, not construction of a new facility (Chambers and Partners, PCC resource pages, ELA law, LNG Prime).

duplicates_confirmed.name_in_press: Shell Energy Philippines Batangas LNG import terminal (2022 revival, 2025-26 NTP/investment news)
duplicates_confirmed.evidence: Shell's DENR-EMB filing and press coverage explicitly describe the project as reviving the Tabangao Realty Inc. (TRI) LNG import terminal first proposed in 2013 at Shell's existing Tabangao facility in Batangas City — the same site GEM tracks as 'Tabangao FSRU / Shell' (shelved) (constructionboxscore, fuelsandlubes, eia.emb.gov.ph ESP PDF, Manila Bulletin May 2025/2026).

duplicates_confirmed.name_in_press: Prime Infra (Enrique Razon) offshore LNG terminal at Batangas (First Gen gas asset acquisition)
duplicates_confirmed.evidence: Prime Infra's Nov 2025 acquisition of 60% of First Gen's gas subsidiaries explicitly includes 'an interim offshore LNG terminal located in Batangas' (60% Prime Infra / 20% First Gen / 20% Tokyo Gas) — this is an ownership change at the existing FGEN Batangas FSRU, not a new terminal (Forbes, Rappler, Milbank, Manila Bulletin, Tribune).

duplicates_confirmed.name_in_press: Energy World Corporation LNG-to-power project, Pagbilao, Quezon (incl. June 2026 turbine-sale/wind-down news)
duplicates_confirmed.evidence: Energy World Gas Operations Philippines' Pagbilao Grande Island LNG storage/regas terminal (3 mtpa, 130,000 m3) is the project GEM already tracks; June 2026 news of Siemens turbine sale confirms it is winding down further, not a new site (energyworldcorp.com, naturalgasworld, aseanenergy.org, lngjournal, theglobeandmail).

duplicates_confirmed.name_in_press: Samat LNG Corp / 'Bataan Open Access LNG Terminal (BOLT)' at PNOC Industrial Park, Limay/Mariveles, Bataan
duplicates_confirmed.evidence: Samat LNG Corp received DOE NTP (Jan 2023) for a 0.2-0.4 mtpa small-scale import terminal at PNOC's industrial park in Limay, Bataan (adjacent to Mariveles); gem.wiki's own 'Mariveles LNG Terminal' page (viewed only for dedup, not cited) lists Samat LNG Corp as 100% owner and cites the same Sept 2023 PNOC lease deal. PNOC's own 'BOLT' branding for this Samat partnership is the identical project, not a second Bataan terminal (PNA, Power Philippines, BusinessWorld, philstar, pnoc.com.ph press release, LNG Prime).

duplicates_confirmed.name_in_press: Phoenix Petroleum / CNOOC Gas and Power 'Tanglawan Philippine LNG' Batangas terminal
duplicates_confirmed.evidence: Direct name match; Phoenix/CNOOC's DOE-approved Batangas regas terminal was branded 'Tanglawan Philippine LNG' and was suspended/shelved after Udenna's Malampaya stake deal — same project GEM tracks as cancelled (constructionboxscore, marinelink, offshore-energy.biz, bworldonline).

duplicates_confirmed.name_in_press: PXP Energy unsolicited 'Integrated Gas Hub' proposal reusing Malampaya facilities
duplicates_confirmed.maps_to_covered: N/A — not a terminal at all; DOE denied the proposal outright
duplicates_confirmed.evidence: PXP's proposal was to reuse the existing offshore Malampaya gas facilities/pipeline network for a domestic gas hub upon SC38 expiry, not to build a new LNG import/export terminal; DOE denied it and PXP's request for reconsideration was also rejected (imoa.ph, businessmirror, naturalgasworld). No marine LNG terminal is implicated; excluded from candidates as not a genuine LNG terminal proposal, not merely a dedup.

Vires Energy withdrew its 2021 DOE NTP for the integrated LNG terminal in Sept 2024, pivoting the associated power plant to pipeline gas instead; GEM already tracks this as cancelled (gem.wiki Vires FSRU page confirms the same NTP/timeline, viewed for dedup only; bworldonline, lngprime, industrialinfo, ieefa).

notes: Ring C covered every named PH LNG developer/upstream-gas-operator in the brief (First Gen/FGEN, AG&P/Linseed Field/Nova, San Miguel Global Power/SMGP, Meralco/MGen, Aboitiz Power, Excelerate Energy, Shell Philippines, Linseed Field Corp, Prime Infra, Vires Energy, PXP Energy/Malampaya consortium) plus PNOC, Samat LNG, Phoenix Petroleum/CNOOC, GNPower, and Energy World Corp as they surfaced. Every lead resolved to one of the 14 already-covered GEM terminals, to a non-terminal proposal (PXP), or to the single vague DOE-secretary reference with no identifiable sponsor (monitor_list). The gem.wiki 'LNG Terminals in Philippines' category was fetched directly (curl with browser UA after WebFetch hit a 403) and contains EXACTLY the 14 pages on the dedup list -- zero gemwiki-only gaps, so the gem.wiki cross-check ring produced no candidates to independently research. Ring D broad sweeps (Visayas/Mindanao regas siting, Bulacan/Zambales/Cavite, FLNG/associated-gas export ideas) turned up no additional named projects; multiple 2025 sources (Reuters/BusinessWorld) confirm DOE's own view that the Philippines is NOT pursuing new Luzon terminals near-term due to excess capacity (only ~60% utilization), and any Visayas/Mindanao siting remains speculative with no developer named. Because no candidate met the tight threshold, no URL required the repo's url_verifier.py pass (that step applies to staged candidate citations); duplicate-confirmation evidence above is drawn from multiple independent press/company/regulatory sources per case and is sufficient to justify NOT staging any of these as Discovery candidates.
summary: No new in-scope Philippines LNG terminal was found: every developer/sponsor lead surfaced by Ring C (First Gen, AG&P/Linseed Field, San Miguel/SMGP, Meralco/MGen, Excelerate, Shell, Prime Infra, Vires Energy, PXP/Malampaya) and Ring D (Samat LNG/PNOC BOLT in Bataan, Phoenix Petroleum/CNOOC's Tanglawan, GNPower's original Mariveles proposal, Energy World Corp's Pagbilao wind-down, and a broad Visayas/Mindanao/FLNG sweep) resolved to one of the 14 terminals GEM already tracks, or in PXP's case to a non-terminal gas-hub reuse proposal that DOE denied. The gem.wiki 'LNG Terminals in Philippines' category, fetched directly for the coverage cross-check, lists exactly the same 14 pages with no additional titles, so the wiki cross-check produced zero gaps to independently research. The only unresolved item is a single vague Oct 2025 DOE-secretary remark about 'one new terminal proposal in the pre-development stage' with no developer or location named in any outlet found; it is logged to monitor_list for a future pass rather than staged, since it fails the tight threshold on named sponsor and concrete step.
